jurisdiction.venue: U.S. District Court for the Central District of California & DOJ Tax

headline: Early Bitcoin Evangelist Resolves Decade-Old Exit Tax Case With a Check and Zero Prison Time
deck: Roger Ver admitted a willful $16.9 million tax loss — prosecutors had once alleged $48 million — and paid $49.9 million to have his indictment dismissed, with zero days in prison.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: Resolved 2014 exit-tax charges via a Sept. 2025 DPA (announced Oct. 14, 2025): admitted a willful $16.9M tax loss, paid $49.9M in tax, penalties and interest, and served zero days in prison.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Underreporting $18,000 in W-2 cash wages on a federal return
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Multi-year criminal tax sentence rarely resolved by a decade-late check with zero incarceration

sources.title: Roger Ver Admits Misconduct and Enters Deferred Prosecution Agreement
sources.agency: U.S. Department of Justice Tax Division / C.D. Cal.

sources.title: Early bitcoin investor charged with tax fraud

interactive_art_spec.caption: Roger Ver, early Bitcoin investor. His deferred prosecution agreement, announced Oct. 14, 2025, ended a federal tax indictment for $49.9 million and zero prison days.
